blocks.explanation: Dekhiye, yeh sawal \(i\) ki power simplify karne ka hai. Given sirf \(i^{9}\) hai, aur humein find yeh karna hai ke yeh chaar values \(1, i, -1, -i\) mein se kaun si hai. Sirf yeh chaar hi kyun? Kyun ke \(i\) ki powers aik cycle (chakkar) mein ghoomti hain: \(i^1 = i\), \(i^2 = -1\), \(i^3 = -i\), \(i^4 = 1\), aur \(i^5\) se wahi silsila dobara shuru ho jata hai, bilkul ghari ki sui ki tarah jo 12 ke baad phir 1 par aa jati hai. Plan: power 9 ko 4 se divide karenge. 4 ke multiple wala hissa 1 ban jayega, aur sirf remainder (baqi) faisla karega ke jawab kya hai.
steps:
Step 1: Power ko 4 se divide karein
\[9 = 4 \times 2 + 1\]
\[i^{9} = i^{8} \cdot i\]
Kyun: Exponent ka qanoon \(a^{m+n} = a^m \cdot a^n\) kehta hai ke jab powers jama ho rahi hon to hum unhein alag alag factors bana sakte hain. 9 ko 8 + 1 likh kar hum \(i^9\) ko do hisson mein tor dete hain: aik hissa \(i^8\) jo 4 ka multiple hai aur aasani se 1 ban jata hai, aur doosra bacha hua \(i\).

Step 2: \(i^{8}\) ki jagah 1 likhein
\[i^{8} = (i^{4})^{2}\]
\[= 1^{2} = 1\]
\[i^{9} = 1 \cdot i = i\]
Kyun: \(i^4 = 1\) hai, is liye \(i^8 = (i^4)^2 = 1^2\). Aur 1 ko jitni baar marzi multiply karein, 1 hi rehta hai. Is tarah 4 ke multiple wala poora hissa jawab par koi asar nahin daalta, aur sirf bacha hua \(i\) jawab ban jata hai.
Dhyan dein: 9 ko 4 se divide karne par quotient (2) aur remainder (1) aate hain. Jawab ke liye sirf remainder dekhna hai, quotient nahin. Bohat se students quotient dekh kar \(i^2\) likh dete hain, jo ghalat hai.

Tasdeeq:
Remainder 1 ho to jawab hamesha \(i\) hota hai: \(i^1 = i\), \(i^5 = i\), \(i^9 = i\). Hamara jawab isi pattern mein fit baithta hai, yani theek hai.
blocks.final_answer: \(i^{9} = i\) (cycle do poore chakkar laga kar wapas \(i\) par aa gaya)

blocks.explanation: Yeh bilkul part (i) jaisa sawal hai, sirf power bari hai. Humein \(i^{17}\) ko \(1, i, -1, -i\) mein se kisi aik value mein badalna hai. Formula yahan wahi cycle wala qaida hai: \(i^4 = 1\), is liye 4 ka har multiple 1 ban jata hai. Plan: 17 ko 4 se divide karke remainder dekhein; wohi batayega ke cycle mein hum kahan khare hain.
steps:
Step 1: Power ko 4 se divide karein
\[17 = 4 \times 4 + 1\]
\[i^{17} = i^{16} \cdot i\]
Kyun: Power mein se 4 ka sab se bara multiple (yahan 16) alag kar lete hain, kyun ke usi hisse ko hum 1 bana sakte hain. Baqi 1 power bachti hai, yani aik \(i\).

Step 2: \(i^{16}\) ki jagah 1 likhein
\[i^{16} = (i^{4})^{4} = 1^{4} = 1\]
\[i^{17} = 1 \cdot i = i\]
Kyun: Qanoon \((a^m)^n = a^{mn}\) se \(i^{16} = (i^4)^4\) likha, aur \(i^4 = 1\) hone ki wajah se yeh \(1^4 = 1\) ban gaya. Ab \(1 \cdot i\) sirf \(i\) hai.
Dhyan dein: \(i^{16}\) ko \(16i\) ya \(4i\) mat samjhein. Power ka matlab baar baar multiply karna hai, number se zarb dena nahin.

Tasdeeq:
Remainder 1 aaya, to jawab \(i^1 = i\) jaisa hi hona chahiye. Hamara jawab \(i\) hai, yani theek hai. Khud sochiye: \(i^{18}\) kya hoga? (Remainder 2, to \(-1\).)
blocks.final_answer: \(i^{17} = i\) (17 ka remainder 1 hai, is liye jawab \(i\))

blocks.explanation: Ab yahan ruk kar dekhiye: is baar base \(-i\) hai, sirf \(i\) nahin. Yahi farq is sawal ki asal baat hai. Given \((-i)^{19}\) hai aur humein isay simple value mein likhna hai. Tareeqa yeh hai ke \(-i\) ko do factors (hisson) mein toren: \(-i = (-1) \cdot i\). Phir dono ki power alag alag nikaalenge, kyun ke \((-1)\) ki power aur \(i\) ki power dono ke apne aasaan qaide hain. Aakhir mein dono results multiply kar denge.
steps:
Step 1: Minus sign ko alag karein
\[(-i)^{19} = ((-1) \cdot i)^{19}\]
\[= (-1)^{19} \cdot i^{19}\]
Kyun: Qanoon \((ab)^n = a^n b^n\) kehta hai ke product ki power lein to har factor ko wohi power lagti hai. Is se aik mushkil cheez do aasaan cheezon mein bant jati hai.

Step 2: \((-1)^{19}\) nikaalein
\[(-1)^{19} = -1\]
Kyun: \(-1\) ko \(-1\) se multiply karein to \(+1\), phir \(-1\) se to \(-1\); yani even (juft) power par \(+1\) aur odd (taaq) power par \(-1\). 19 odd hai, is liye \(-1\).

Step 3: \(i^{19}\) nikaalein
\[19 = 4 \times 4 + 3\]
\[i^{19} = i^{16} \cdot i^{3}\]
\[= 1 \cdot (-i) = -i\]
Kyun: \(i^{16} = (i^4)^4 = 1\), aur bachi hui power 3 hai. \(i^3 = i^2 \cdot i = (-1)i = -i\). Yani cycle mein teesri value \(-i\) hai.

Step 4: Dono results multiply karein
\[(-i)^{19} = (-1)(-i)\]
\[= i\]
Kyun: Minus ko minus se multiply karein to plus banta hai, is liye \((-1)(-i) = +i\).
Dhyan dein: Bohat se students \((-i)^{19}\) ko seedha \(-(i^{19})\) samajh lete hain. Odd power par yeh sahi nikalta hai, lekin even power par ghalat ho jata hai: \((-i)^2 = -1\), jab ke \(-(i^2) = +1\). Hamesha \((-1)\) ki power alag nikaalein.

Tasdeeq:
\(-i\) ki powers ka apna cycle hai: \((-i)^1 = -i\), \((-i)^2 = -1\), \((-i)^3 = i\), \((-i)^4 = 1\). 19 ka remainder 3 hai, aur is cycle ki teesri value \(i\) hai. Dono tareeqon se jawab aik hi aaya.
blocks.final_answer: \((-i)^{19} = i\) (minus ki odd power ne sign aik baar aur palat diya)

blocks.explanation: Yeh is sawal ka sab se tricky hissa hai, is liye dhyan se. Power negative bhi hai aur fraction bhi: \(-21/2\). Sab se pehle humein yeh pehchanna hai ke half power (\(1/2\)) ka matlab square root hai, aur \((-1)^{1/2} = \sqrt{-1} = i\), jo iota ki definition hai. Is liye hum expression ko \(i\) ki power mein badal lenge: \((-1)^{-21/2} = ((-1)^{1/2})^{-21} = i^{-21}\). Phir negative power ko positive banayenge, \(i^{21}\) ko cycle se simplify karenge, aur aakhir mein \(i\) ko denominator (neeche) se nikaalenge.
steps:
Step 1: Power ko \((1/2) \times (-21)\) likhein
\[(-1)^{-\frac{21}{2}} = \left((-1)^{\frac{1}{2}}\right)^{-21}\]
\[= (\sqrt{-1})^{-21}\]
\[= i^{-21}\]
Kyun: \(-21/2\) ko hum \((1/2) \times (-21)\) likh sakte hain, aur \((a^m)^n = a^{mn}\). Half power ka matlab square root hai, aur definition se \(\sqrt{-1} = i\). Pehle square root lena hi kitab ka tareeqa hai, aur isi se sahi jawab aata hai.

Step 2: Power ko positive banayein
\[i^{-21} = \dfrac{1}{i^{21}}\]
Kyun: Qanoon \(a^{-n} = 1/a^{n}\): negative power ka matlab hai ke cheez neeche (denominator mein) chali jaye aur power positive ho jaye. Positive power ko cycle se simplify karna aasaan hai.

Step 3: \(i^{21}\) simplify karein
\[21 = 4 \times 5 + 1\]
\[i^{21} = (i^{4})^{5} \cdot i = i\]
Kyun: 4 ka multiple wala hissa \(i^{20} = (i^4)^5 = 1\) hai, aur remainder 1 ki wajah se sirf aik \(i\) bachta hai. Ab expression \(1/i\) ban gaya.

Step 4: Denominator se \(i\) nikaalein
\[\dfrac{1}{i} = \dfrac{1}{i} \cdot \dfrac{i}{i}\]
\[= \dfrac{i}{i^{2}} = \dfrac{i}{-1}\]
\[= -i\]
Kyun: Jawab ko simple complex number banane ke liye neeche \(i\) nahin rehna chahiye. Upar neeche \(i\) se multiply karne se value nahin badalti (\(i/i = 1\)), lekin neeche \(i^2 = -1\) aa jata hai jo aam real number hai. \(i\) ko \(-1\) se divide kiya to \(-i\).

Aam ghalti (Common mistake)
Pehle power \(-21\) mat lagayein: \(((-1)^{-21})^{1/2} = (-1)^{1/2} = i\) aa jata hai, jo alag (ghalat) value hai. Negative number ki fractional power mein tarteeb (order) se farq parta hai, is liye hamesha pehle \(-1\) ka square root lein, jaise kitab karti hai. Doosri aam ghalti: \(1/i\) ko \(i\) samajh lena. Yaad rakhiye, \(1/i = -i\) hai.

Tasdeeq:
\[i \cdot (-i) = -i^{2} = 1\]
Agar \(-i\) waqai \(1/i\) hai to \(i\) se multiply karke 1 aana chahiye, aur 1 hi aaya. Jawab theek hai.
blocks.final_answer: \((-1)^{-\frac{21}{2}} = -i\) (pehle square root se \(i\) bana, phir power aur reciprocal ne isay \(-i\) kar diya)
